description.name: Plain
description.purpose: Plain is an API-first B2B support platform that consolidates customer conversations from email, Slack, Microsoft Teams, chat, Discord, and product channels into threads, with queue management, automation, customer context, help-center features, and AI agents.

evidence.excerpt: Plain is a support platform for B2B teams, built API-first so you can change how it works rather than work around it.
Customer conversations arrive from email, Slack, Microsoft Teams, chat, Discord, or your own product, and become threads in a single queue that your team and your AI agents both work from.

methods.method: API key passed as a Bearer token
setup_steps: Go to Settings → Machine Users and click + Add Machine User.
Click Add API key and select the required fine-grained permissions.
Copy the key when created; Plain will not show it again after leaving the page.
Send it as the Authorization: Bearer plainApiKey_xxx header.
scopes: Fine-grained permissions; documented examples include thread:read, thread:reply, generatedReply:create, thread:assign, thread:unassign, and customer:read.

evidence.excerpt: Create a machine user and an API key, and scope it with fine-grained permissions.

methods.method: OAuth 2.0 for the official Plain MCP server
setup_steps: Point an MCP client at https://mcp.plain.com/mcp.

evidence.excerpt: Pinterest API services are only available to authenticated and authorized users.
The Pinterest API supports three grant types, which are methods for authenticating your app and acquiring authorization to access protected resources.

Scopes table
Entity  | `read` permissions  | `write` permissions
`ads`  | See all data related to advertising, such as ads, ad groups and campaigns.  | Create, update or delete ads, ad groups and campaigns.
`billing`  | See all of your billing data, such as your billing profile.  | Create, update or delete billing data.
`biz_access`  | See all business access data.  | Create, update or delete business access data.
`boards`  | See public boards, including group boards, with `boards:read` or secret boards with `boards:read_secret`.  | Create, update or delete public boards with `boards:write` or secret boards with `boards:write_secret`.
`catalogs`  | See all catalog data.  | Create, update or delete catalogs.
`pins`  | See public pins with `pins:read` or secret pins with `pins:read_secret`.  | Create, update or delete public pins with `pins:write` or secret pins with `pins:write_secret`.
`user_accounts`  | See user accounts and followers.  | Update user accounts and followers.

setup_steps: Create an app and API account in the BigCommerce Developer Portal.

scopes: OAuth scopes are resource- and action-based, including read-only, modify, create, get, token-login, and token-generation permissions; examples include store_v2_orders, store_v2_customers, store_storefront_api, and account_read.

evidence.excerpt: BigCommerce uses a modified version of the OAuth2 authorization code grant.

BigCommerce offers three types of OAuth-based API accounts to developers who wish to use BigCommerce’s REST APIs: store-level credentials, app-level credentials, and account-level credentials.

methods.method: Access token in the X-Auth-Token header
setup_steps: Create a store-level, app-level, or account-level OAuth API account.

scopes: The token's OAuth scopes determine permitted resources and actions.

description.name: Ecwid
description.purpose: Cloud ecommerce platform for creating online stores, managing products, orders, customers, payments, shipping, inventory, and selling across websites, social platforms, marketplaces, and point-of-sale channels.

evidence.excerpt: Ecwid provides all the tools you need to create a professional online store and grow your ecommerce business.

From the Ecwid admin, you can manage your products, orders, and customer profiles, connect preferred payment methods, set up flexible shipping or delivery methods, customize product pages and website, and even purchase a domain name.

methods.method: OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow with bearer access tokens
setup_steps: Register an external application.
Have the merchant install and authorize the application.
Exchange the temporary authorization code at the Ecwid OAuth token endpoint using client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, and grant_type=authorization_code.
Use the returned access_token as the bearer credential for REST API calls.

evidence.excerpt: External applications work outside of Ecwid control panel and they also have an app details page for easy installation process. These apps use oAuth2 flow to get access token for a specific Ecwid store.

scope | List of permissions (API access scopes) given to the app, separated by space.

methods.method: Bearer access token using a custom application's secret or public token
setup_steps: Create or open a custom application in the Ecwid admin app dashboard.
Copy the generated secret or public access token from the app Details page.
Send the token in the Authorization header as a Bearer token.

evidence.excerpt: After signing up with Ecwid and getting a custom app, you already have two tokens: Public token allows only public data to be received and is safe to use in public code. description.name: Amazon Selling Partner
description.purpose: Amazon's REST-based Selling Partner API lets selling partners and authorized applications programmatically access and exchange data for Amazon selling operations such as catalog, listings, orders, fulfillment, reports, payments, and notifications.

evidence.excerpt: The SP-API offers a collection of REST-based APIs that you can use to automate selling operations such as order processing, shipment tracking, and payment management.

methods.method: OAuth 2.0 through Login with Amazon (LWA), using bearer access tokens; restricted operations use Restricted Data Tokens (RDTs)
setup_steps: Register an application.
Obtain LWA client ID and client secret from the developer console.
Authorize the application by a selling partner, or self-authorize a private application.
Exchange the authorization refresh token for an LWA access token.
For restricted operations, obtain and use an RDT instead of an LWA access token.

evidence.excerpt: The authorization method is either OAuth 2.0 (for public applications) or self-authorization (for private applications):
A Login with Amazon (LWA) access token authorizes your application to take certain actions on behalf of a selling partner.

When calling restricted operations, instead of including an LWA access token, you include a Restricted Data Token (RDT).

description.name: Apify
description.purpose: Cloud platform for web scraping, data extraction, browser automation, and related workflows built around serverless Actors that accept structured input and produce stored results.

evidence.excerpt: Apify is a cloud platform for web scraping, data extraction, and automation. Everything on it revolves around Actors - serverless programs that run in the cloud.
Actors are serverless cloud programs that take a structured JSON input, perform a task (web scraping, browser automation, data processing, and more), and optionally produce a structured output.

strict_mcp_servers.name: Datadog MCP Server
strict_mcp_servers.access_restrictions: Uses Datadog user authorization and existing RBAC/resource permissions. Remote authentication supports OAuth 2.0; header authentication supports PAT, SAT, or API/application keys. Organization administrators can manage global MCP access and write capabilities; IP allowlists may restrict connections.

setup_steps: Register a client application using Smartsheet Developer Tools to obtain a client ID and client secret.
Redirect the user to Smartsheet's authorization endpoint with the requested scopes.

evidence.excerpt: Developer Tools is a Smartsheet user interface for registering client applications that use OAuth to access Smartsheet user resources with the user's consent.

description.name: Harvest
description.purpose: Time tracking and project-management software for tracking hours against client projects, analyzing project and team performance, and invoicing clients.

evidence.excerpt: Everything your team needs to keep track of hours and projects
In Harvest, all time is tracked to a task that’s assigned to a project for a client. You can then use that tracked time to analyze projects, manage your team, and invoice your clients.

setup_steps: Sign in to Harvest ID.
Open the Developers section.
Create a Personal Access Token and record the returned account IDs.
Send the token in the Authorization: Bearer header and the account ID in Harvest-Account-Id.

evidence.excerpt: The API can be accessed by creating a Personal Access Token from the Developers section of Harvest ID. After creating it you’ll be provided with a random token and a list of your account IDs.
Personal Access Tokens have the `all` scope by default, so you have full access to all of your accounts.

setup_steps: Register an OAuth2 Application in the Developers section of Harvest ID with a name, redirect URL, account mode, and requested products.
Use the Authorization Code flow for server-side applications or the Implicit Grant flow for client-side applications.
Exchange an authorization code for access and refresh tokens, or receive an access token through the implicit flow.
Use the bearer access token for Harvest API requests and refresh it when required.

evidence.excerpt: If you are interested in building integrations that other users can use, you will need to register an OAuth2 Application, also known as an OAuth2 Client.
We use the Authorization Code flow for server-side applications.
We use the Implicit Grant flow for client-side applications.
The `scope` can contain one or more of these values: `harvest:{ACCOUNT_ID}`, `forecast:{ACCOUNT_ID}`, `harvest:all`, `forecast:all`, and `all`.
